reason: This passage (Exodus 14) describes Yahweh's salvation of the Israelites from the pursuing Egyptian army. While the Israelites express fear and doubt about their circumstances, the text does not depict Yahweh as angry at the people. Instead, Yahweh responds to their distress with deliverance and miraculous intervention—parting the sea, protecting them from the Egyptians, and drowning Pharaoh's army. The passage concludes with the people believing in Yahweh and Moses, indicating a positive relationship. There is no indication of the people failing to worship Yahweh properly, nor any expression of divine anger on those grounds. The narrative is one of salvation and demonstrated divine power, not divine punishment for improper worship.
